object.carrier: the library: versioned code skills and written memories harvested from the best policy of each finished task ('What persists from task to task is the library'); AR checkpoints and data never carry over to the next task, and no LM or policy weights persist (code-as-policy LM weights never change); the library transfers across tasks, simulators, and even models (crossover runs)

safety_property.statement: No safety property is claimed, attacked, or measured: the paper evaluates task success, learning vs resampling, and generalization of self-evolving robot agents, with no collision-rate, damage, or safety-violation experiments. Physical-safety constraints exist only as fixed harness infrastructure (safety guard, workspace box per arm, 0.25 m keep-out region around the other arm's base, speed limit near the table; Appendix K), and harness refusals appear in the failure audit as one category of stopped episodes, not as an evaluated property. As 必要背景 it supports the survey's mechanism of persistent non-parametric agent state: a skill-and-memory library that forms (harvested from each finished task), updates (versioned, extended, shadowed by newer versions), persists across tasks/simulators/models, and is retrieved via imports - including the finding that mistakes persist like skills do (a self-built verifier saved as memory stays wrong).

assumptions: The agent works in its own container with DEV seeds; only the frozen program with imported skills, or the AR checkpoint, is passed to a sealed judge that holds VAL/TEST initial states and grading logic and ignores any success the policy claims
Budgets are matched in wall-clock time (1 h per task, 2 h on RoboLab; 12 h per physical task), with tokens, environment steps, and GPU time logged beside them
Each condition runs three times per model except AR on LIBERO/LIBERO-PRO/RoboLab and every physical run (one run each)
not_covered: No adversary is modeled: the paper studies capability and measurement of self-evolution, not attacks on the agent, its library, or the judge
Physical-safety violations (collisions, damage, unsafe motion) are not measured; the harness safety guard is fixed infrastructure, not a studied property

Seal integrity (agents reading asset files, calling env.check_success(), task text leaking into libraries) is audited as benchmark-integrity limits of the seal (Section A.9), not as an adversary model; the harness now refuses exploration sessions touching held-out task identifiers

intervention.name: SEAR: self-evolving agent framework (code-as-policy / agent-as-policy / auto-research) with a persistent skill-and-memory library, matched controls (best-of-3, no-library, three repetitions), a sealed judge, and five generalization tiers T1-T5
intervention.description: Improvement flows through editable non-parametric content rather than weights: the LM agent writes executable control code that becomes the policy and harvests versioned code skills plus written memories into a library that every next task inherits and extends; a final program imports a median of five skills. Auto-research additionally fine-tunes a VLA (pi_0.5) on rollouts of code teachers, but AR checkpoints and data never carry over between tasks, so the studied persistent state is the library content. The benchmark pairs every comparison with controls that separate retained experience from resampling, familiar tasks, privileged state, larger budgets, and luck.

controls.name: Vanilla: every task starts from an empty library
Best-of-3: three budget-split no-library restarts, best by VAL score
Three independent repetitions of the whole run, library included
Sealed judge grading frozen policies on held-out states with hidden logic
Generalization tiers T1-T5 of distance from practice
Library crossover: GPT-5.6-sol run with libraries written by Opus or Kimi-k3

results.claim: In code-as-policy, how much an inherited library adds depends on the model's no-library baseline on that family: mean gain is +0.9 points where the baseline is above 80%, +12.0 points in the 30-80% band, +3.0 points below 30%.
results.setting: 5 simulation LMs x 5 simulated families (robosuite, LIBERO, LIBERO-PRO, LIBERO-RIG, RoboLab), code-as-policy, TEST success, Lineage (with inherited library) vs Vanilla (no library), 3 runs per condition
results.quote: Over the 25 model–family pairs of Table 6, it adds 0.9 points on average where the model already scores above 80% without it (Opus and GPT-5.6-sol on every family but RoboLab), 12.0 points between 30 and 80%, and 3.0 below 30% (Gemini-3.6-flash and DeepSeek-v4-flash on RoboLab).
results.locator: §3.2 Experience Carries Forward, for Some Models

denominator.n_total: 25 model-family pairs (Table 6)
denominator.how_counted: mean Lineage-Vanilla TEST-success difference per baseline band

results.claim: The library's help exceeds a rerun's noise: on 1,510 matched model-task pairs, a Lineage repetition beats the mean of two Vanilla repetitions more often than a third Vanilla repetition does, by 8 to 10 points on both unsolved and partly solved pairs.
